title: 2-representation theory of the Taft algebra
summary: We study the $2$-representation theory of the Taft category, the tensor category of finite-dimensional modules over the Taft algebra. This category has two left cells. We first classify suitable transitive modules over its based representation ring. For the upper cell, we recall a construction by Etingof and Ostrik giving an infinite family of pairwise nonequivalent simple $2$-representations. For the bottom cell, we pass to the semisimplification of the Taft category and identify a distinguished fusion subcategory with an adjoint $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Verlinde category. Using algebra objects associated with $\mathsf{ADET}$-diagrams and categorical Clifford theory, we classify the regular exact indecomposable module categories of this semisimplification. For these regular module categories, the split Grothendieck group is a complete invariant. Finally, we identify the two cell $2$-representations of the Taft category.

title: Spherical harmonics and infinitesimal projective transformations
summary: Consider the space of $C^\infty$-functions on the two-dimensional sphere $S^2$ and its decomposition $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ into a direct sum of minimal rotation-invariant spaces. We consider elements of $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ as functions of two variables, a nonnegative integer variable $m$ and a complex variable $u$ (a restriction of such function to a set $m=k$ is a polynomial in $u$ of degree $\le 2k$). The group $\mathrm{GL}\,(3,{\mathbb R})$ of all matrices of order 3 acts on $S^2$, so its Lie algebra acts in $C^\infty(S^2)$ by differentiations along vector fields. We construct operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$ corresponding such differentiations and obtain a collection of differential-difference operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$. The expressions include shifts $m\mapsto m\pm 2$ and derivatives of order 4 in $u$.

title: Oscillator representations of quantum affine orthosymplectic superalgebras II
summary: As a continuation of our study on quantum affine spin-oscillator correspondence, we introduce a category of $q$-oscillator representations of quantum affine superalgebras of type $XB$ ($X=B,D$) and construct irreducible objects in a uniform way. Under the truncation functor inspired by the theory of super duality, they are related to finite-dimensional irreducible representations of $U_q(D^{(2)}_{n+1})$ ($X=B$) or $U_q(B^{(1)}_{n})$ ($X=D$). We also considerably streamline our previous arguments, which clarifies how our construction can be understood as a quantum affinization of classical super duality.

title: Divisors on regular Hessenberg varieties for h=(2,3,4,...,n,n) associated to lower subsets
summary: For a regular Hessenberg variety associated to the Hessenberg function $h=(2,3,4,\ldots,n,n)$, we construct Cartier divisors $D_A$ associated to lower subsets $\emptyset\subsetneq A\subsetneq[n]$. We show that their first Chern classes satisfy the quadratic relations suggested by the combination of the works of B$\breve{\text{a}}$libanu-Crooks and Horiguchi-Masuda-Shareshian-Song. We also give a characterization of these divisors in terms of the centralizer action. It also follows that these divisors generate the (pseudo)effective cone of divisors on the Hessenberg variety.

title: Real Nullstellensatz for nilpotent Lie algebras
summary: We prove a real Nullstellensatz for the universal enveloping algebra U(g) of a nilpotent finite-dimensional real Lie algebra g: An ideal of U(g) is real if and only if it is the intersection of kernels of irreducible integrable *-representations of U(g) by (in general unbounded) operators on a Hilbert space. For this, we build upon some classical results about the complexification of U(g) that lead to a complex Nullstellensatz (every semiprime ideal is the intersection of primitive ideals), but focus only on the ``real points'', i.e., the *-representations on Hilbert spaces. On the technical side, this requires to take into account an involution of U(g), namely, the antipode of its Hopf algebra structure, which goes into the definition of real ideals of U(g). Our result is the first noncommutative real Nullstellensatz for *-algebras with unbounded irreducible *-representations, demonstrating how methods of real algebraic geometry can lead to results about operator *-algebras also in situations where C*-algebraic methods fail.

title: Harder-Narasimhan Filtrations of Hyperquiver Representations
summary: Hyperquiver representations are generalisations of quiver representations. They are directed hypergraphs with vector spaces assigned to vertices, and for every directed hyperedge, an assignment of a linear map from the tensor product of the source vector spaces to the tensor product of the target vector spaces. We study the moduli of hyperquiver representations, where we use affine GIT to describe the (in)stability of such objects under the action of a product of general linear groups. Our main result introduces the Harder-Narasimhan filtration of a hyperquiver representation. We also derive a formula for the weights of this unique filtration, which specialise to the Harder-Narasimhan slopes of a quiver representation.

title: Elements of the Green ring related to Alperin's weight conjecture
comment: Submitted to Journal of Algebra August 30,2026
summary: J. L. Alperin introduced his celebrated weight conjecture, a major question in the modular representation theory of finite groups, which has now been studied for several decades. Alperin viewed this conjecture as the beginning of a ``Lie theory for the general finite group", as the title of the article indicates. This paper is intended as a tribute to Alperin's insight. In this note, we place an emphasis on projective modules and putting the numerical questions arising from the weight conjecture into a ``module form" within the appropriate Green ring of RG, when G is a finite group, and R is a suitable complete discrete valuation ring with residue field of prime characteristic p. We believe that this work moves in the direction of a structural approach to Alperin's weight conjecture.

title: Supercuspidal blocks and the local Langlands correspondence
summary: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group defined over a non-archimedean local field $F$, and let $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$ be a supercuspidal Bernstein block. In this paper, we define a cohomology class $[μ_{\mathfrak{s}}]$ represented by a 2-cocycle that encodes the equivalence class of $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$. We then formulate a conjecture describing $[μ_{\mathfrak{s}}]$ in terms of the enhanced $L$-parameter $(\varphi, ρ)$ attached to an irreducible representation in $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$ via the conjectural local Langlands correspondence. Finally, we verify this conjecture for the local Langlands correspondence for non-singular supercuspidal representations constructed by Kaletha.

title: Lie algebras in symmetric tensor categories
summary: We develop the general theory of Lie algebras in symmetric tensor categories. We prove categorical versions of classical results such as Engel's theorem, Cartan's criterion, and that all derivations of a strongly semisimple Lie algebra are inner. For finite-dimensional graded Lie algebras, we construct a graded category $\mathcal{O}$, classify its graded-simple objects, and prove the generic graded irreducibility of Verma modules. Lastly, we develop the theory of root systems for contragredient Lie algebras.

title: Generic distinction of induced representations: the case of symmetric spaces
summary: Let H be the fixed-point subgroup of an involution of a reductive group G over a local field F of characteristic zero. We give a necessary condition for a parabolically induced representation of G(F) to admit a non-zero family of H(F)-equivariant linear forms depending holomorphically on the induction parameter. By works of Blanc-Delorme and Brylinski-Delorme, this condition is essentially sufficient. As a global consequence, we obtain vanishing results for regularized periods of Eisenstein series. We illustrate this on symplectic periods, where we extend Offen's computation of truncated periods of certain cuspidal Eisenstein series to inner forms of GL(2n).

title: Approximability of Triangulated Categories under Separable Extensions
summary: In this paper, we investigate the behavior of approximability under separable extensions of triangulated categories. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be an approximable triangulated category and let $\mathbf{T}$ be a smashing, stably separable exact monad on $\mathcal{B}$. We prove that if $\mathbf{T}$ is right $t$-exact with respect to a $t$-structure in the preferred equivalence class, then the category of $\mathbf{T}$-modules $\mathbf{T}\text{-Mod}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is again an approximable triangulated category. As an application, we show that, under suitable assumptions, a smashing localization functor on an approximable triangulated category induces a recollement of approximable triangulated categories, thereby yielding a converse-type result to the gluing theorem of Burke--Neeman--Pauwels. Finally, we prove that separable extensions restrict naturally to the intrinsic subcategories associated with approximable triangulated categories.

title: Uniqueness of twisted linear periods
summary: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero, and let $\D$ be either $F$ or a quaternion division algebra over $F$. We prove that every irreducible smooth representation of $\GL_{p+q}(\D)$ has at most one linear period transforming under any prescribed character of $\GL_p(\D)\times\GL_q(\D)$.

title: Eigenvectors of $p$-Curvature for Geometric Difference Equations
summary: A qKZ-type additive discrete flat connection in characteristic $p$ has $p$-curvature operators. They are commuting automorphisms of the connection. We present a Bethe-ansatz-type construction of eigensections and eigenvalues of the $p$-curvature operators. An eigensection of $p$-curvature operators is a discrete hypergeometric sum over the finite lattice $\mathbb{Z}^r/p\mathbb{Z}^r$. Thus, the $p$-curvature eigensections are constructed by a finite, discrete analogue of a hypergeometric integral.

title: Monodromy Eigenvectors for Difference Equations with Root-of-Unity Step
summary: A qKZ-type discrete flat connection with multiplicative step $p$ has monodromy operators when $p$ is a root of unity. The monodromy operators are commuting endomorphisms of the connection. We construct their eigensections and eigenvalues. The construction is based on the presentation of the discrete flat connection as a discrete Gauss-Manin connection.

title: Sharp Threshold for Universality of Rational Canonical Forms over a Finite Field
comment: This paper supersedes arXiv:2510.16225. 15 pages. Comments welcome!
summary:
We study the rational canonical form of sparse random matrices over a finite field. Suppose $A_n\in\mathrm{Mat}_n(\mathbb{F}_p)$ has independent and $α_n$-balanced entries. We prove that if $nα_n-\log n\to+\infty$, then, for every fixed collection of distinct monic irreducible polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_p$, the corresponding primary partitions of $A_n$ converge jointly to the same asymptotically independent Cohen-Lenstra distributions as in the uniform random matrix model. This strengthens the finite-field cokernel universality theorem of Lee (arXiv:2511.13070), which assumes $α_n=c\log n/n$ for a fixed $c>1$, by resolving the additive endpoint case explicitly left open in his work. Moreover, our result extends universality from ordinary cokernels to the full rational canonical form. The condition is optimal for universality uniformly over fixed irreducible polynomials.
  Our proof uses the surjection moment method developed by Sawin and Wood (arXiv:2210.06279) over $\mathbb{F}_p[t]$, together with a refinement of Lee's Fourier estimates that retains the full leading-order decay. We also construct degree-$d$ critical sparse obstructions, suggesting a polynomial-dependent threshold of $1/d$ for irreducible polynomials of minimal degree $d$.

title: A Littlewood-Richardson Rule for Forest Polynomials
comment: 28 pages. v2: the Schubert bialgebra material of v1 has been split off into the companion paper arXiv:2610.22582; this version contains the forest Littlewood-Richardson rule, reorganized from what was the final section of v1, with the needed background collected in Section 2. Title changed
summary: The forest polynomials $\mathfrak{P}_a$ of Nadeau-Tewari form a $\mathbb{Z}$-basis of $\mathbb{Z}[x_1,x_2,\ldots]$ whose role for the cohomology of the quasisymmetric flag variety parallels that of Schubert polynomials for the classical flag variety. Nonnegativity of the structure constants $β_{a,b}^c$ in $\mathfrak{P}_a \mathfrak{P}_b = \sum_c β_{a,b}^c \mathfrak{P}_c$ is known, but no Littlewood-Richardson-style enumerative rule has been available. We give such a rule: $β_{a,b}^c$ counts pairs of forest RC graphs of forest-codes $a$ and $b$ whose lift product lands on a forest RC graph of forest-code and weight both equal to $c$. The same rule descends to the cup product on $H^\bullet(\mathrm{QFl}_n)$. The proof introduces a squash product $\boxtimes$ on RC graphs, which on full Grassmannian RC graphs of a fixed height recovers the plactic monoid, a multiplactic algebra $\mathcal{M}_n$ that models Schubert polynomial multiplication, and a lift product $*$ on RC graphs whose quasi-crystal structure, in the framework of Cain-Guilherme-Malheiro, transports the Nadeau-Tewari forest equivalence through the computation. The row-decomposition machinery on RC graphs that underlies these constructions is developed in a companion paper.

title: A note on complex Lie Algebras isomorphic to their conjugate
summary: A real Lie algebra defines by extension of scalars a complex Lie algebra that is isomorphic to its Galois conjugate. In this paper, we are interested in the converse property: given a complex Lie algebra that is isomorphic to its conjugate, is it defined over the real numbers? We prove the existence of a $10$-dimensional nilpotent complex Lie algebra for which the answer is negative, disproving a recent conjecture by Deré. In addition, we compute the generic obstruction to this descent problem in terms of Brauer groups.

title: Affine diagram categories, algebras and monoids
comment: 29 pages, many figures, comments welcome; to appear in J. Algebra
summary: We introduce and study several affine (=annular in this paper) versions of the classical diagram algebras such as Temperley-Lieb, partition, Brauer, Motzkin, rook Brauer, rook, planar partition, and planar rook algebras. We give generators and relation presentation for them and their associated categories, study their representation theory, and the asymptotic behavior of tensor products of their representations in the monoid case. Under a mild hypothesis, we also prove a previous conjecture concerning the asymptotic growth of the number of indecomposable summands in the tensor powers of representations for finite monoids.

title: Extremal monomials of $q$-characters
summary: In this short paper, we prove a conjecture of Frenkel-Hernandez, which states that $q$-characters of finite-dimensional simple modules of the quantum affine algebra $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{g}})$ are bounded by the Weyl group orbit of the leading monomial under Chari's braid group action. This can be regarded as a (partial) quantum affine generalization of the Weyl group invariance of characters of finite-dimensional representations of $\mathfrak{g}$.

title: Representing Vineyard Modules
summary: Time-series of persistence diagrams, more commonly known as vineyards, are a useful way to capture how multi-scale topological features vary over time. However, we do lose significant information in how the persistent homology at different time stamps relate to each other. A natural algebraic version of vineyards is a time series of persistence modules equipped with interleaving maps between the persistence modules at different time stamps. We call this a vineyard module. In this paper we will set up the framework for representing a vineyard module via an indexed set of vines alongside a collection of matrices. We outline an algorithmic way to transform the bases of the persistence modules at each time step within the vineyard module to make the matrices within this representation as simple as possible. With some reasonable assumptions on the vineyard modules, this simplified representation can be completely described (up to isomorphism) by the associated vineyard and a vector of finite length. While this vineyard and vector representation is not necessarily unique we can prove that the vector will always be the zero vector when the vineyard module is isomorphic to the direct sum of vine modules. We also show uniqueness when the vineyard module contains two vines (over field $\mathbb{F}_2$) and can characterise and count which are realisable, giving a complete account of isomorphism classes of vineyard modules with two vines. To define and analyse this approach we first must set up a lot of preliminary results about changes of bases for pairs of persistence modules where we are given $\varepsilon$-interleaving maps for sufficiently close $\varepsilon$. This new perspective on vineyards also provides a new approach to the study of multi-parameter persistence modules.
